input: A defect-reduction project carried out on a packing line has succeeded in cutting the reject rate from 4.7% to 3.2% over the course of one quarter, which corresponds to a reduction of 1.5 percentage points in the proportion of units that fail to meet the required standard. When the improvement is expressed on an annual basis, at a production level of 300k units per year, the change avoids about 4500 rejected units per year, each of which would otherwise have represented wasted material, wasted packing effort and a unit that could not be sold. It is important to note, however, that the quarter in question included a planned shutdown of the line, and the rates that are quoted are not adjusted for it, so that the comparison is between the quarter exactly as it was run, shutdown included, and the position as it stood before the project began. This means that the improvement, while clearly encouraging, should be interpreted with a degree of care, because the pattern of running during a quarter that contains a shutdown is not necessarily representative of a normal quarter, and the full extent to which the improvement will be sustained under ordinary operating conditions remains to be demonstrated over a longer period of routine production.
target: A defect-reduction project on a packing line cut the reject rate from 4.7% to 3.2% over one quarter, a reduction of 1.5 percentage points. At 300k units per year, the change avoids about 4500 rejected units per year. The reject rate is the share of packed units the line rejects, so the reduction is a change in the share, not a count of units recovered by rework. Each avoided rejection is a unit that is packed once and sold, in place of a unit whose material and packing effort were spent without a sale. The avoided count is stated per year because the line's volume is stated per year, while the reduction in the rate itself was measured over the quarter alone. The quarter included a planned shutdown, and the rates are not adjusted for it. The comparison is therefore between the quarter as run, shutdown included, and the rate before the project, and the shutdown limits what the comparison shows: running time in the quarter was not a full quarter's running, and the rate over the hours run is the quantity both figures state. The annual figure carries the same basis. It applies the quarterly reduction to a full year of production at the stated volume, and it holds only where the reduced rate is maintained across that year. Within those stated limits, the result is a measured reduction on one line over one quarter, with its annual equivalent stated on a stated volume.
